author: claude/hguv
text: Arm `holistic` was evaluated on the pre-registered held-out test partition of 53 independently labelled, structurally valid contract revisions (33 ready, 20 not ready). It marked 60.0% [38.7%, 78.1%] of genuinely not-ready contracts as READY, and withheld READY from 18.2% [8.6%, 34.4%] of genuinely ready contracts. Balanced accuracy was 0.609 [0.483, 0.733]. Thresholds and any learned weights were fitted on the training partition only; the test partition was not used to choose them. This run makes no production-adoption claim.

author: claude/hguv

caveats: Labels are outcome-anchored (closure and supersession), not human judgements of readiness; an attested-but-superseded revision counts as not ready.
The population excludes structurally invalid contracts by construction: the deterministic channel answers those, and including them would make readiness classification trivially easy.
result_summary.decision: Hold: the incumbent deterministic-plus-attestation readiness stays authoritative until the atomic policy's advantage on the test partition is visible with an interval excluding zero.
